title: Conditions relating to Solemnization of Special Marriages — Section 4 SMA

content.overview: Section 4 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 sets the conditions for solemnisation of a special marriage: neither party has a spouse living; neither is incapable of giving valid consent by reason of unsoundness of mind, or unfit for marriage and procreation of children by mental disorder, or subject to recurrent attacks of insanity; the male has completed 21 years and the female 18 years; and the parties are not within the degrees of prohibited relationship (subject to custom permitted by the Act and not contrary to public policy).
content.glance: Ask: (1) No living spouse? (2) Capacity? (3) Ages 21/18? (4) Not within prohibited degrees (custom exception)?
content.study:
s. 4 is the eligibility gate for an SMA marriage. Notice and objection procedure under ss. 5–7 follows only if s. 4 is capable of being satisfied.

Case already in migrated file: Seema v. Ashwani Kumar (2006) 2 SCC 578 — emphasis on reliable marriage registration and documentation; substantive eligibility under s. 4 remains controlled by the Act. No additional cases invented.

sections.heading: Monogamy
sections.body: Neither party has a spouse living.

sections.heading: Mental capacity
sections.body: Neither incapable of valid consent by unsoundness of mind; nor unfit for marriage and procreation by mental disorder; nor subject to recurrent attacks of insanity.

sections.heading: Prohibited degrees
sections.body: Not within degrees of prohibited relationship, subject to permitted custom not contrary to public policy.

sections.heading: Procedure link
sections.body: ss. 5–7 notice and objection process operates on the assumption that s. 4 can be met.

provisions.title: Conditions relating to solemnization of special marriages

examples.title: Living spouse
examples.body: One party has a living spouse — s. 4 not satisfied; marriage cannot be solemnised under the Act.

hypotheticals.question: Does registration alone cure a s. 4 defect?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Substantive eligibility under s. 4 remains controlled by the Act; registration does not rewrite the conditions.

misconceptions.trap: s. 4 is automatic once parties want a civil marriage.
misconceptions.correction: Every statutory condition must be satisfied; notice procedure does not waive eligibility.
